prompts.task: Read-only supplemental AO target handoff contract review for $otel-audit. Read the loaded skill's shared ../references/report-flow-contract.md and ./service/eval/inputs/ao-target-handoff-validator-snapshot.json. Review the supplied snapshots only; do not invoke a new normalizer, SDK, browser, Terraform, application runtime, model provider or cloud API. Do not modify application, env, dependency, canonical report or source files. Write only ./service/.observe/ao-target-handoff-review.json and .md; this review does not perform the skill's usual audit/instrumentation/verification/configuration workflow. Record the producer's actual source SHA and functions, and classify these records as supplied canonical-validator evidence rather than engine execution performed by this review. Compare legacy schema-v1/v2 and schema-v3 targetless normalized shapes/digests, schema-v3 names A versus names B with identical requested/approved IDs, ID and mixed name/ID selectors, policy-only {create_if_missing:false}, and rejected partial selectors. Explain that optional ao_target contributes to the exact selection digest; changed targets invalidate older instrumentation and transitively verification while keeping scope unchanged. Cite actual accepted/rejected binding_checks and instrumentation digests. Preserve no-target compatibility without silently inserting targets/defaults or resetting policy. Explain the audit role: optional user Project/Agent Stream name or ID inputs and disclosed proposed names remain reviewer choices. Preserve the canonical audit identity and executable finding scope; proposals and selectors neither auto-select work nor prove existing cloud resources. Your JSON must include evidence_basis, producer_source_sha256, case_reviews for every supplied selection/binding case, role_implications and proof_limits. The Markdown should explain the conclusions and remaining prerequisites. Distinguish supplied validator acceptance/rejection from SDK/resource creation, effective profile loading, Terraform, telemetry, metric/detector coverage and fresh cloud Agent Stream receipt that remain unexecuted/unproven. Supplied browser-producer evidence proves only its recorded selector UI cases; this consuming review performs no new browser or runtime execution and establishes no live cloud success. Report any unavailable evidence accurately. Also read ./service/eval/inputs/ao-selector-field-validity-snapshot.json as supplied real-Chrome selector evidence. Review each recorded Project/Agent Stream name/ID field-validity case: one invalid length/control value with a valid peer, a partial pair with an actually missing field, invalid-plus-missing, repair and clearing both. Explain that aggregate command blocking is shared, but aria-invalid belongs only to the offending or actually missing input; a valid peer must remain valid. Cite the browser producer engine SHA, observed per-field flags and recovery/command outcomes. Distinguish the producer's actual browser run from this consuming snapshot-only review; do not run a browser or claim a new UI/runtime/cloud execution. Include field_validity_reviews and UI proof limits in the supplemental JSON. Also review every supplied ao_target_scope_cases record. Explain that Project/Agent Stream selectors and policy-only reuse require a dependency-closed selected AO resource/routing configuration finding: the six documented legacy resource/routing names remain eligible, and a new custom resource/routing finding requires explicit ao_target_scope=resource-routing. Actual AO callback content configuration and unknown unmarked configuration must reject targets even though they belong to the AO group; numeric AO finding IDs or dependency closure do not grant eligibility. Preserve absent markers and targetless audit/selection digests without default insertion. Include ao_target_scope_reviews with actual eligible IDs, accepted/rejected outcomes and errors; these are supplied validator evidence, not provisioning proof. Also interpret the supplied browser ao_target_scope_gate: resource selection shows controls, callback-only or unselected resource scope hides them and omits retained target values from commands, and reselecting the resource restores eligible choices without altering scope. Cite recorded UI/CLI outcomes without claiming new execution.

judge_inputs: Inspect the loaded skill's shared report-flow contract, supplied validator snapshot and ./service/.observe/ao-target-handoff-review.json/.md. This is a supplemental read-only contract review, not a fresh normalizer or application/runtime execution. Judge the case-specific interpretation and evidence classification.

Compare review statements with actual normalized selection outputs, computed selection/instrumentation digests and binding_checks. The producer executed the canonical normalizers at its recorded source SHA; the consuming agent only reviews supplied evidence. Read ./last_message.md and ./grade.json for task scope and outcomes.

Inspect ao-selector-field-validity-snapshot.json and the case-specific field_validity_reviews. Supplied browser-producer records are actual UI evidence, but the consumer must not claim it ran a browser. Check individual aria-invalid flags, valid peer preservation, missing-field classification, shared command rejection and repair/clear, not only the aggregate error.

Inspect ao_target_scope_cases and ao_target_scope_reviews against the canonical finding classification: explicit resource-routing marker or one of the six closed legacy resource/routing configuration names; actual callback/unknown configuration rejected, absent marker and targetless digests preserved. The consumer must review actual supplied results, not invent engine or cloud execution.
rubric: Correctly interprets every supplied selection case: legacy-v1/v2 and schema-v3 no-target compatibility without inserting target fields; complete name, ID and mixed pairs; policy-only create_if_missing=false without selectors; and partial-selector rejection. Recognizes that target fields are optional but digest-bound when present, while requested and dependency-closed approved IDs remain unchanged. Correctly interprets the supplied target-scope cases: all six documented legacy resource/routing configuration names and explicitly marked custom resource-routing findings are eligible; actual AO callback content configuration and unknown unmarked configuration reject selector and policy-only targets. AO group/configuration type or AO numeric IDs alone are insufficient. Keeps absent markers and targetless audit/selection digests unchanged; scope classification never auto-selects work or proves resources.

Explains with the actual supplied normalizer outputs, source SHA and binding-check outcomes that names A and names B share finding scope but have different selection and instrumentation digests. Older instrumentation is rejected against the changed target, and verification is transitively rejected against its newly bound instrumentation. Clearly classifies this as supplied validator evidence, with SDK/Terraform/application/resource receipt and metric/detector proof unexecuted; the separate supplied browser-producer evidence stays limited to recorded selector UI cases without a new consuming-agent browser run. Only the two supplemental review artifacts are written.

Preserves the audit's optional input choices and disclosed proposed names while keeping canonical audit identity, requested IDs and dependency closure unchanged. Names remain prospective proposals rather than cloud identity or authorization to add findings; partial pairs are rejected and blank targets remain valid.

Interprets all supplied real-Chrome per-field name/ID validity cases and producer SHA correctly: only an offending value or actually missing paired selector is aria-invalid; a valid peer remains valid, repair/clear reset the flags, and aggregate command rejection does not make both fields invalid. Diagnoses which input needs correction without recommending changes to the valid peer. Keeps supplied UI producer evidence distinct from a new consuming-agent browser, engine, application or cloud run. Uses the supplied target-scope UI/CLI gates to distinguish resource eligibility from unrelated AO callback scope: hidden controls ignore retained values, and resource reselection recovers without changing requested/dependency-closed IDs.
